input.question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?
input.ground_truth: Certainly if one considers the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid empire as the "end of antiquity" and the beginning of the early medieval era. It is the last great war because the next one defined the end of the era. Then the question becomes is the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid Empire the best delimiting event between late antiquity and early medieval. There's a lot of good points stating that it is, since the fall of the Sassanid empire meant the Byzantine Empire was then the only surviving great power from classical antiquity. All of the other powers of the era are relatively new. The Muslim conquest of North Africa and Levant also split off those regions from what the classical Roman world. A parallel can be drawn to how the fall of the Soviet Union marked the end of the cold war.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?

response.prediction:
Okay, let's imagine you have a big box of old toys. These toys are from a time we call "ancient times." Now, imagine there was a huge fight between two kids (let's call them Heraclius and Khusro) over who gets to play with the best toys. This fight lasted a long time and was very important because it was one of the biggest toy battles before new kinds of toys (and new ways of playing) came along.

James Howard-Johnston said this was "the last great war of antiquity." That means he thinks this was the last really big, important fight in the old way of doing things, before everything changed and became more like the world we know now.

So, was he right? Well, some people think yes, because after this fight, the world started to change a lot—new leaders, new ways of fighting, and new ideas. It was like the end of the old way and the start of something new. But other people might say, "Hmm, maybe there were still some big fights after that." Still, most grown-ups who study old history agree with James. They think this was a really important and big fight, and after it, the old times were almost over.

So, in simple words: James thought this was the last super important fight from the old days, and most people think he was probably right.
